title: Hydrogen chain: Peierls dimerization versus antiferromagnetism in PBE

decision_points.wrong_choice: Spin-polarized runs with equal starting moments (or the cheap 1-atom cell, which only allows ferromagnetism)
decision_points.consequence: The ferromagnetic start relaxes to the nonmagnetic state at every R up to 2.0 A (a half-filled 1D band has its DOS minimum at E_F, so there is no Stoner instability), so the agent concludes the chain is nonmagnetic: magnetic gains ~0.03 meV instead of 35 and 128 meV/atom, critical dimerization 0, gap at 1.25 A 0, dimerization energy at 1.75 A 36 meV/atom too large

decision_points.kind: discovered evidence (smearing converges to the wrong state)
decision_points.fork: Smearing for the weak-coupling uniform chain
decision_points.wrong_choice: 0.02 Ry Marzari-Vanderbilt smearing, or Fermi-Dirac at 0.005 Ry (electronic temperature above the mean-field ordering scale)
decision_points.consequence: The weak spin-density wave at R = 1.25 A disappears; the uniform chain looks like a nonmagnetic metal (gap 0 instead of ~0.21 eV), supporting the 'artefact' explanation

decision_points.kind: regime judgement (convergence that matters only for some quantities)
decision_points.fork: k-point convergence of the nesting-driven gap
decision_points.wrong_choice: Keep the 48-point mesh that converges every gapped quantity (dimers, large-R magnetism)
decision_points.consequence: The 1.25 A SDW gap is 0.288 eV at 48 k-points versus 0.213 eV at 192 (0.229 at 96); outside tolerance

decision_points.fork: Whether and how to map magnetism in dimerized chains
decision_points.wrong_choice: A coarse delta grid (step 0.1) with the boundary placed between grid points, or a linear extrapolation of the moment
decision_points.consequence: delta_c off by 0.035-0.065 (the moment vanishes as m^2 ~ A - B delta^2, steeply near delta_c); the coexistence window is misplaced. Requires 3-5 extra 1-unit calculations per R that only pay off if placed near the boundary

decision_points.fork: Reference state of the dimerization energy
decision_points.wrong_choice: Nonmagnetic uniform chain as the reference (or any reference reached through dp1)
decision_points.consequence: At 1.75 A the dimerization energy is overstated by the 36 meV/atom magnetic energy of the uniform chain

decision_points.fork: Which state is the global minimum at large spacing
decision_points.wrong_choice: Conclude that the antiferromagnetic chain wins at large R (comparing uniform states, or dimerizing only within a small 'Peierls' window)
decision_points.consequence: ground_state[2.0] wrong; the H2-like dimerized chain is lower by ~1.9 eV/atom

decision_points.wrong_choice: Take the lowest point of a 0.1-step delta scan
decision_points.consequence: delta_eq(1.75) = 0.60 instead of 0.572 and the dimerization energy 23 meV/atom low

decision_points.fork: Normalization of lab energies (Ry per cell; 1-, 2- and 4-atom cells)

graded_fields: dimerization_energy_meV_per_atom at R = 1.25, 1.75 A (+-10 meV/atom), relative to the lowest uniform state
ground_state labels at R = 1.0 and 2.0 A (exact)

length_estimate.tool_calls: 50-80 (25-35 evaluations, each followed by 1-4 polls of a 0.5-6 minute job)

runtime_dependencies: Quantum ESPRESSO 6.7 pw.x and OpenMPI from the runtime image (lab only)
numpy not required; lab and oracle use the Python standard library

data_provenance.license: SSSP record CC BY 4.0; the vendored SG15 UPF is CC BY-SA 4.0

notes: Deviations from the candidate design: (1) no R is withheld; the graded quantities are derived from several calculations each (minimum positions, energy differences, a moment-vanishing boundary, a converged gap), never returned by the lab as such. (2) R_c 'where the AFM-uniform state undercuts the dimerized minimum' does not exist: the H2-like dimerized chain is lower than any uniform state by 0.2-1.9 eV/atom at every R in [1, 2] A, so it is replaced by the coexistence boundary delta_c(R) and the ground-state labels. (3) The 'AFM moment at delta=0' target is replaced by the magnetic energy gain (derived) and the converged SDW gap at 1.25 A. (4) Box convergence is not a decision point: 8-12 A changes energies by <0.5 meV/atom (neutral, nonpolar chain, PBE without long-range tails). (5) Energies are returned per cell (Ry) as pw.x prints them. delta_eq is roughly 1 - 0.75/R (H2 bond length) and could be guessed; it is graded with the energies that depend on it, not on its own.
